terms.gloss: sing to deaf ears: talk in vain
evidence: Verg. Ecl. 10.8: nōn canimus surdīs (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 40.8.10: quae vereor nē vāna surdīs auribus cecinerim (Lewis & Short s.v. canō)
terms.comment: The deaf ears stand in the dative, with no preposition.

evidence: Ov. Am. 3.7.61 (Lewis & Short s.v. cantō: “to preach to deaf ears”)
terms.comment: Traupman’s form, with ad. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

terms.gloss: we are not singing to the deaf

phrases.latin: quae vereor nē vāna surdīs auribus cecinerim
phrases.english: which I fear I have sung in vain to deaf ears

sources: Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
Lewis & Short: surdus · Lewis & Short: cano · Lewis & Short: canto
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 96, 255, 301, checked against the searchable text and the page images of the book.
